messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: P00042 - edge-network-health spike (TLS handshake errors + 5xx at edge). Severity: P2. Affected: EU and US-east edge clusters. Links: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/P00042 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Triggered by multiple 5xx anomalies from edge-proxy (avg TLS failures 18% over 5m) — paging oncall (maria)

maria: ack — oncall, looking now. Any first-order customer reports?

ajay: seeing elevated 523/525 from synthetic checks hitting eu-west edge. Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.example/d/edge/handshake-errors 

kevin: confirmed spike correlated with new cert rotation deployment to edge-proxy in eu-west ~ 00:07 UTC. Rolling back cert job now.

maria: good call. kevin can you paste the rollout command?

kevin: ```
# rollback cert rotation
kubectl -n edge set image deploy/edge-proxy edge-proxy=registry/redwood/edge-proxy:stable-20250314
kubectl rollout status deploy/edge-proxy -n edge
```

sarah: I'm seeing Route53 change logs showing a partial TTL update for canary weight shift at 00:05 UTC. Might be a propagation mismatch between regions. DNS query failures -> fallback to other edge -> TLS mismatch -> handshake failure chain.

maria: ok prioritize rollback + weight shift to us-east-primary to reduce eu traffic. ajay, run weight shift and confirm client-facing access.

ajay: starting weight shift via traffic-router api: `POST /v1/route/shift {"from":"eu-west","to":"us-east","pct":80}` — will ramp over 60s.

incident-bot: Auto-note: traffic-router policy applied by ajay at 00:12 UTC. Estimated shift complete by 00:13 UTC.

kevin: rollback in progress, pods restarting. `kubectl get pods -n edge | grep edge-proxy` shows new pods becoming Ready.

maria: checking auth-proxy -> edge backend TLS handshake traces: I see client hello offered TLS1.3 vs server older cipher, handshake aborted with ALERT_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE. That matches a cert/key mismatch at the edge-proxy.

sarah: route53 health-checks still show failures for a subset of IPs. I'm going to remove 3 target IPs from ALB target group temporarily. Doing: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:... --targets Id=i-abc123`

ops-bot: Runbook step executed: deregister problematic targets (step 3). Logging to incident timeline.

maria: good. ajay, after weight shift completes, can you run a small synthetic query set against eu and us endpoints to validate? Use the /healthz + TLS handshake checks.

ajay: running curl matrix now:
```
for region in eu-west us-east; do
  curl -I -s --resolve "api.redwood.example:443:$region_ip" https://api.redwood.example/healthz || echo "fail $region"
done
```

ajay: us-east OK, eu shows intermittent TLS handshake failures ~ 5/20. Traffic shift down to 15% eu now.

maria: customer impact: support reports a handful of customers in EU seeing increased 5xx and chat connections dropped. Tier1 on CS notified. I'm drafting a short status update.

kevin: backup: rotated certs just before incident for compliance push. Looks like one node got a malformed chain uploaded. I'll run checksum across all hosts and remove bad cert.

sarah: Route53 TTL still sticky on some resolvers. I'm contacting DNS provider to confirm propagation path for the problematic records.

pagerduty: Escalation: sending to SRE lead (sarah) if not resolved in 15m.

maria: summary of actions so far: 1) kevin rolling back cert deployment; 2) ajay shifted traffic to us-east; 3) sarah deregistered bad targets; 4) ops-bot logged runbook steps. Next: verify cert consistency, re-register healthy targets, and gradually restore traffic.

kevin: checksum script: ```
ssh edge@host "sha256sum /etc/ssl/certs/edge-cert.pem"
# comparing against signed artifact list
```

kevin: found host i-0badcert with mismatched sha, replacing with artifact copy and restarting edge-proxy on that host.

maria: monitoring error% graph... errors dropping from 18% -> 3% after weight shift + deregister. Good signal.

ajay: traffic ramp to eu 40% to test — no regression for 2m. Continuing.

incident-bot: Incident update: service degradation mitigated, customer impact reduced. Recommend follow-up postmortem and ticket to improve cert rollout validation and add preflight sha check.

maria: creating incident ticket and assigning to eng-runtime for postmortem: INC-6202. Will include timeline and suggested action items.

sarah: will open DNS propagation follow-up with provider; also adding runbook step to detect TTL drifts earlier.

kevin: will add preflight cert checksum + canary verify step to deployment pipeline.

maria: thanks all. I will send short status to #customers and close PD after 30m of stable metrics. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty: Alert acknowledged and escalations cleared by maria at 00:35 UTC.

maria: final note: no data loss, limited customer impact (short-lived 5xx for EU customers). Postmortem owner assigned. Closing thread once INC-6202 is created and CS update posted.

ops-bot: Post-incident checklist queued: notify legal if customer SLA threshold exceeded, update runbook, schedule blameless postmortem session.
